description: MATHEMATICS: theorem, proof, algebra, geometry, calculus, number, function — a timeless / universal-region anchor. Cornelius Vane the Victorian holds it as fully as a modern mathematician.

microtheory.name: mathematics
microtheory.definition: The timeless study of number, quantity, structure, space and change, built by proof from axioms: algebra, geometry, calculus, logic, topology. A universal world present in every frame — Vane's age knew Euclid, Newton and Gauss.

concepts.name: theorem
concepts.definition: A statement proved true by deduction from axioms and prior theorems.

concepts.name: proof
concepts.definition: A finite chain of valid inferences establishing a theorem beyond doubt.

concepts.name: algebra
concepts.definition: The study of operations and their structure over symbols standing for numbers.

concepts.name: geometry
concepts.definition: The study of points, lines, figures and space, and their measure.

concepts.name: calculus
concepts.definition: The study of continuous change via derivatives and integrals.

concepts.name: number
concepts.definition: An abstract quantity — natural, integer, rational, real or complex.

concepts.name: function
concepts.definition: A rule assigning to each input of a domain exactly one output.

concepts.name: equation
concepts.definition: A statement that two expressions are equal, to be solved or verified.

concepts.name: topology
concepts.definition: The study of properties preserved under continuous deformation.

concepts.name: logic
concepts.definition: The formal study of valid inference and the structure of proof.

concepts.name: set
concepts.definition: A collection of distinct objects considered as a single mathematical whole.

concepts.name: integral
concepts.definition: The accumulated total of a quantity — the area under a curve.

concepts.name: derivative
concepts.definition: The instantaneous rate of change of a function.

concepts.name: axiom
concepts.definition: A statement taken as self-evidently true, the starting point of a proof.

concepts.name: prime
concepts.definition: A natural number greater than one divisible only by one and itself.

concepts.name: matrix
concepts.definition: A rectangular array of numbers representing a linear map or system.

concepts.name: probability
concepts.definition: The measure of how likely an event is, between zero and one.

concepts.name: group
concepts.definition: A set with an associative operation, identity and inverses — the algebra of symmetry.

concepts.name: limit
concepts.definition: The value a function or sequence approaches as its input approaches a point.

concepts.name: series
concepts.definition: The sum of the terms of a sequence, finite or infinite.
